sources.news_title: Sex trafficking brothers learn fate months after Aussie victim dies
sources.text:
Alon, Tal and Oren Alexander – three brothers who once lived at the height of wealth and society in New York and Miami – were each sentenced to 30 years in federal prison Tuesday for sex trafficking and other crimes after facing several of their victims during an emotional, hours-long hearing.
“These men spent years treating women and girls as though our lives, body, voices, humanity meant nothing,” a victim using the pseudonym Katie Moore said in court. “But we are not disposable and they are not untouchable.”
Moore was one of 12 women who delivered statements Tuesday in a federal courtroom in Manhattan packed with victims and their supporters for the sentencing of the three brothers, who were convicted earlier this year of sex trafficking, conspiracy to commit sex trafficking and other charges.

The sentencing marks a dramatic fall from grace for the three men: Tal, 40, and Oren, 39, were top luxury real estate brokers, while Alon, Oren’s twin, was an executive at their family’s security company.
Numerous accusers came forward after Australian woman Kate Whiteman sued Oren and Alon for allegedly sexually assaulting her in 2012. Whiteman died near Sydney in late 2025, months before the beginning of the five-week trial.
Prosecutors laid out evidence demonstrating the brothers’ yearslong pattern of using their wealth and social status to lure women to luxury locations before using drugs or force to rape and sexually assault them – many of whom were unconscious or several incapacitated.
Eleven women testified at trial about being sexually assaulted by one or more of the men, though prosecutors said more than 70 women had reported their accounts to investigators.
Federal district judge Valerie Caproni likened the three brothers to Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde.
In letters to the court, the men’s supporters described them as gentlemen, while the women who testified credibly at trial described “sadistic, misogynistic sexual predators,” she said.
“Either all of those women are in the wrong line of work because they should all be actresses, or they were telling the truth and they were raped and drugged. And I credit latter,” the judge said before handing down the sentences.
The brothers, wearing beige prison outfits, each addressed the court and acknowledged being ashamed of their behavior but vehemently maintained they never drugged or raped anyone.
“I want to set the record straight – my brothers and I have never drugged and raped anyone. Have never trafficked anyone for sex. Have never conspired to harm anyone,” Oren said Tuesday, as several victims shook their heads.
As she sentenced the men, Caproni said she believed that was “entirely a lie.”
“Your conduct was monstrous,” the judge said.
All three men were also convicted of inducement to travel for unlawful sexual activity. Alon and Tal were also convicted of sex trafficking a minor.
The twins were convicted of additional sex abuse counts and the jury also found Oren guilty of sexual exploitation of a minor.
Their defense attorneys had asked the judge to issue the lowest possible sentence of 15 years, saying the men were interested in “meeting women” when they were younger but are now dedicated fathers needed by their families.
“The defendants really left the conduct on their own,” Marc Agnifilo, a defense attorney for Oren , said. “All three defendants stopped and that matters.”
Federal prosecutors, meanwhile, argued the men deserved life in prison, the maximum possible sentence, due in part due to the callousness with which they committed their crimes.
“These attacks were often relatively brief, an hour in an evening, and then after they were done, the defendants were able to laugh about it, brag about it, and move on with their lives,” Elisabeth Espinosa, an assistant US attorney for the Southern District of New York, said.
“The victims were left picking up the pieces, dealing with the shattering grief, the confusion, the pain of what the defendants had done to them, and what didn’t matter to the defendants.”
The US Attorney for the Southern District of New York said in a statement after the sentencing the brothers preyed on young women and girls for years and used their social status to their advantage.
“Today’s sentence makes clear that this craven, sinister conduct is extraordinarily serious and will be met with serious punishment,” US Attorney Jamie McDonald said in the statement.
‘I grieve the girl that I was’
Before they were sentenced, the Alexander brothers listened to a dozen women who described being preyed upon by the defendants. Some of the women dabbed their eyes or fought back tears; others urged the judge to hand down a sentence of life in prison.
One woman, who said she was raped by two of the brothers and their friends when she was a teenager, said she still has flashbacks more than a decade after the assault.
“I cry for the innocence of that terrified 16-year-old and stand for her today,” said Isa Brooks, who spoke using a pseudonym. “Their eyes went black. As if I was being mauled by animals.”
“I grieve the girl that I was,” she said.
Brooks – who was one of the eleven women who testified against the brothers at trial – said she eventually reported the attack out of fear there were more women at risk, and she was in “utter shock” to learn how many other victims there were.
Another victim who used a pseudonym, Maya Miller, said in court Tuesday she will “forever carry the scars” of being raped by one of the brothers in August 2014. Tal invited her to a mansion in the Hamptons where he trapped her in a bathroom and violently raped her while she pleaded with him to stop, prosecutors wrote in their sentencing memorandum.
“What happened to me was a choice made for me, not by me,” Miller said as she held back tears. “What Tal Alexander did to me was a life sentence that I never asked for. Tal has fundamentally changed the way I experience being alive.”
Ava Wells, who also testified under the pseudonym at trial about being raped by Alon in Tel Aviv in March 2016, said the moment that broke her during the trial was seeing a video of her former self during a playful moment.
“In it, my face was glowing, like there was a light inside me I had completely forgotten was ever there,” she said.
“Suddenly memories of who I used to be came flooding back. Seeing her completely undid me. Like a flash, the realisation sank in and all I could think was: Alon stole her from me.”
A woman identified as Olivia Lane, who did not testify at trial, said Tuesday Oren showed a “complete disregard for (her) humanity” when he raped her in 2015. Lane said she felt unwell after she had a few sips of a margarita while at a party.
“The next thing I remember is waking up to being raped,” she said.
“He did not destroy me, but he should be held fully accountable for what he did. I’m here because I survived him, and I’m here because I remember.
“Whatever they thought power is, is a joke,” Lane said before directly addressing the three defendants.
“You are weak. You are inhumane. You never had power and look at you now.”
Lindsey Acree – who prosecutors say was drugged, forcibly raped and sexually assaulted by Tal in 2011 – said a sentence of life in prison “doesn’t even begin to cover it.”
“Why do we have to be here? Why do I have to be here looking at these guys? I would like to move on,” Acree said, prompting applause from the rows of victims and their supporters seated in the courtroom.
“I’m going to walk out of this room and I hope something I did made some difference.”
‘Please have mercy on me, your honour’
The three defendants stood before Caproni to make their final pleas for mercy, telling the judge they were ashamed of some of their past conduct but were innocent of the charges brought against them.
“There’s one thing I need to tell you and I want to be absolutely clear – I have never not once in my life drugged a woman or had sex with a woman knowing they had been secretly drugged,” Alon said.
“I’m not a perfect man, but I’m innocent of these charges,” he said.
He wiped tears from his eyes as he talked about the difficulty of being separated from his daughters, saying his life now is vastly different than when the charged conduct occurred.
“I’m not telling you I became a flawless person – I’m telling you I changed,” Alon said. “It happened years before my arrest.”
His twin, Oren, said he was “greatly ashamed” of some of his previous actions and was on a “bad path” before he met his wife.
“I was partying too much and sleeping with too many women during those years until I found the most beautiful inside and out perfect woman, the one I wanted to be the mother of my kids and my soulmate for life,” he said.
Tal told the judge he was a different person now, and he wished he had “shown more maturity and been more thoughtful” in the past.
“I hope your honour can understand how difficult it is to stand here, facing the possibility of spending the rest of my life in prison, trying to find words to express genuine regret without confessing something I did not do,” he said, his voice quivering as he spoke of a potential life sentence.
“I’m asking you to please consider my whole life, my family and the possibility of my future beyond this case,” Tal said.
“Please have mercy on me, Your Honour.”

sources.news_title: Real Estate Brothers Tal, Oren and Alon Alexander Get 30 Years in Sex-Trafficking Case
sources.text:
Three brothers once known as rising stars of New York luxury real estate were each sentenced to 30 years in prison Tuesday for running a yearslong sex-trafficking scheme that prosecutors say victimized dozens of women.
U.S. District Judge Valerie E. Caproni imposed the sentences on Tal Alexander, 40, and his twin brothers, Oren and Alon Alexander, 39, in federal court in New York.
A federal jury convicted the three in March of conspiracy to commit sex trafficking, inducement to travel to engage in unlawful sexual activity, and multiple counts of sex trafficking by force, fraud or coercion.
Prosecutors had pushed for life sentences for each brother, while defense attorneys argued for the 15-year statutory minimum.
In a court filing, prosecutors alleged the brothers had raped or sexually assaulted at least 70 women, calling them “serial rapists.” During the four-week trial, 11 women testified against the brothers, including some who said they were minors at the time of the encounters. They described being showered with gifts, flown to parties and other destinations, and given drugs before being assaulted.
Eleven accusers spoke in court Tuesday before sentencing, describing lasting harm from the assaults, according to The Associated Press.
“It took one night, only a few hours, one invitation to completely wreck the girl I once was,” one woman, identified by a pseudonym, told the court, the AP reported.
Lindsey Acree testified that Tal Alexander and another man raped her at a Hamptons home in 2011 after she drank something that left her feeling paralyzed.
“The biggest thing is why? Why did you do this?” Acree said, according to the AP. “I don’t understand the cruelty. I don’t understand the hatred towards women.”
In his closing argument at trial, prosecutor Andrew Jones told jurors the brothers had built an image as wealthy party boys while preying on women.
“They used a consistent playbook to lure, isolate and rape their victims,” Jones said. “They did it with callousness and a perverse sense of pride.”
The brothers denied the sex-crime allegations throughout the trial, with their attorneys arguing the encounters were consensual and accusing prosecutors of overreach. Before sentencing Tuesday, each brother addressed the court and again denied drugging or raping anyone.
“I am not here to discount what they have said,” Oren Alexander said of the accusers. “My brothers and I have never drugged or raped anyone. We never trafficked anyone for sex and we never conspired to hurt anyone.”
Oren said he regretted some of his past behavior toward women but maintained he and his brothers were innocent of the crimes for which they were convicted.
Before their arrests in 2024, Oren and Tal Alexander had built prominent careers in luxury real estate, rising through the ranks at Douglas Elliman and brokering major deals, including the nearly $240 million sale of a penthouse in 2019 that was then the most expensive residential sale in U.S. history. They later co-founded the luxury real estate firm Official in 2022. Alon Alexander worked instead as an executive at the family’s private security company.
Court filings previously obtained by Fox News Digital alleged the brothers used “the promise of luxury experiences, travel, and accommodations” to lure women to locations where they were assaulted. Prosecutors said the alleged abuse stretched back more than two decades, to when the brothers were in high school in Miami.
After the March verdict, U.S. Attorney Jay Clayton described the brothers’ conduct as “calculated, brutal sexual abuse that, unimaginably, the defendants celebrated.”
All three brothers had been held without bail since their 2024 arrests and remained in custody through Tuesday’s sentencing.

NEW YORK, Oct 27 (Reuters) – Three brothers convicted of exploiting their access to wealth and high society in New York and Miami to drug and rape women were each sentenced on Tuesday to 30 years in prison.
The twins Alon Alexander and Oren Alexander, 39, and Tal Alexander, 40, were sentenced by US District Judge Valerie Caproni in Manhattan, seven months after being convicted in a six-week trial of multiple sex crimes including conspiracy to commit sex trafficking.
Lawyers for the brothers did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
• Caproni called the brothers’ conduct “monstrous,” according to multiple media reports.
• Oren and Tal Alexander were co-founders of the luxury real estate brokerage Official, while Alon Alexander was an executive at his family’s security company Kent Security.
• Prosecutors sought life sentences, while the Alexanders requested mandatory minimum 15-year prison terms.
• Prosecutors said the brothers for at least 14 years exploited their social status to prey on women and girls, with more than 70 women saying they were assaulted by one or more of the brothers in locations including Manhattan, the Hamptons on New York’s Long Island, and Aspen, Colorado.
• In one instance, prosecutors said in January 2017 three girls were celebrating their senior year in high school at an Aspen nightclub when the brothers drugged them, enticed them to their five-star hotel for a promised after party, and then assaulted them.
• New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said in a statement provided by the US Attorney’s office in Manhattan, which prosecuted the Alexanders: “With today’s sentencing, they will finally face the consequences they deserve for the incredible harm they inflicted on so many.”
(Reporting by Jonathan Stempel in New York; Editing by Edmund Klamann)

The sentencing marks a dramatic fall from grace for the three men: Tal, 40, and Oren, 39, were top luxury real estate brokers, while Alon, Oren’s twin, was an executive at their family’s security company.

“Your conduct was monstrous,” the judge said.

Their defense attorneys had asked the judge to issue the lowest possible sentence of 15 years, saying the men were interested in “meeting women” when they were younger but are now dedicated fathers needed by their families.
“The defendants really left the conduct on their own,” Marc Agnifilo, a defense attorney for Oren Alexander, said. “All three defendants stopped and that matters.”
Federal prosecutors, meanwhile, argued the men deserved life in prison, the maximum possible sentence, due in part due to the callousness with which they committed their crimes.
“These attacks were often relatively brief, an hour in an evening, and then after they were done, the defendants were able to laugh about it, brag about it, and move on with their lives,” Elisabeth Espinosa, an assistant US attorney for the Southern District of New York, said.

Ava Wells, who also testified under the pseudonym at trial about being raped by Alon Alexander in Tel Aviv in March 2016, said the moment that broke her during the trial was seeing a video of her former self during a playful moment.
“In it, my face was glowing, like there was a light inside me I had completely forgotten was ever there,” she said. “Suddenly memories of who I used to be came flooding back. Seeing her completely undid me. Like a flash, the realization sank in and all I could think was: Alon stole her from me.”

Whatever they thought power is, is a joke,” Lane said before addressing the three defendants. “You are weak. You are inhumane. You never had power and look at you now.”

“Why do we have to be here? Why do I have to be here looking at these guys? I would like to move on. I’m going to walk out of this room and I hope something I did made some difference,” Acree said, prompting applause from the rows of victims and their supporters seated in the courtroom.
Brothers proclaim their innocence
The three defendants stood before Caproni to make their final pleas for mercy, telling the judge they were ashamed of some of their past conduct but were innocent of the charges brought against them.
“There’s one thing I need to tell you and I want to be absolutely clear – I have never not once in my life drugged a woman or had sex with a woman knowing they had been secretly drugged,” Alon Alexander said.
“I’m not a perfect man, but I’m innocent of these charges,” he said.
He wiped tears from his eyes as he talked about the difficulty of being separated from his daughters, saying his life now is vastly different than when the charged conduct occurred.
“I’m not telling you I became a flawless person – I’m telling you I changed,” Alon Alexander said. “It happened years before my arrest.”

“I was partying too much and sleeping with too many women during those years until I found the most beautiful inside and out perfect woman, the one I wanted to be the mother of my kids and my soulmate for life,” he said.
Tal Alexander told the judge he was a different person now, and he wished he had “shown more maturity and been more thoughtful” in the past.
“I hope Your Honor can understand how difficult it is to stand here, facing the possibility of spending the rest of my life in prison, trying to find words to express genuine regret without confessing something I did not do,” he said, his voice quivering as he spoke of a potential life sentence.
“I’m asking you to please consider my whole life, my family and the possibility of my future beyond this case,” Tal Alexander said as some victims in the courtroom held their heads in their hands. “Please have mercy on me, Your Honor.”
Prior to issuing the sentences, Judge Caproni spoke directly to the brothers, calling their conduct “shameful and degenerate” and referencing days of testimony from victims who described “misogynistic sexual predation on the part of all three defendants.”
“Your crimes wreaked havoc on their lives. It has caused long lasting damage to them. Many have significant problem trusting people,” the judge said.
She dismissed the brothers’ apparent attempts to classify their actions as a part of party culture and lambasted their attorneys’ filings ahead of sentencing, which described their behavior as “insensitive.”
“Not just insensitive. It was wrong. Here the wrong was that you drugged, raped and trafficked women, not that you were rude,” Caproni said. “Until each defendant comes to terms with what he did, he poses a risk.”

MANHATTAN (CN) — Socialite brothers Oren, Alon and Tal Alexander were sentenced to 30 years in prison on Tuesday following their all-count convictions on sex trafficking crimes.
The trio was found guilty of raping multiple women between 2009 and 2017, including 11 who testified during their five-week trial earlier this year. Prosecutors said the brothers followed a consistent “playbook,” using their wealth and influence to lure women to their properties, drug and assault them.
Some women testified the brothers raped them by force despite pleas to stop. Others said they were too inebriated to speak.
The brothers did not testify in their defense.
Pleading to the judge for mercy on Tuesday, the trio maintained their innocence. Oren Alexander said plainly that “my brothers and I have never drugged or raped anyone.” He and Alon Alexander each claimed they took polygraph tests to that effect at the start of the case.
“I am innocent of these charges,” Alon Alexander insisted.
But U.S. District Judge Valerie Caproni said this was just another example of the defendants failing to take responsibility for their “monstrous” behavior. She scrutinized Alon Alexander for evidence that came to light during trial of him boasting about having sex with a teenager.
“You were bragging about raping a 17-year-old girl,” the Barack Obama appointee said. “It’s a really good example of how shameful and degenerate your conduct was.”
When addressing the judge, Oren Alexander acknowledged the popularity of the Howard Stern Show and Playboy magazine during his formative years as a young man. Caproni found it to be part of a broader, unsuccessful, effort by the Alexanders to pin their conduct on “hookup culture.”
“That’s not what this was,” she said, criticizing the apparent two-facedness of the defendants by comparing them to Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde.
Caproni’s ruling came after 11 women gave victim impact statements to the court Tuesday morning. Several women described the brothers’ eyes going “black” during assaults. One compared being gang raped by four men, including two of the brothers, to “being mauled by animals.” Another described having such persistent nightmares after her run-in with the defendants that she sometimes screams in her sleep.
These statements showed how the Alexanders “wreaked havoc” on the lives of young women they encountered during their sex trafficking spree, Caproni said.
Each brother’s 30-year sentence will be followed by 10 years of supervised release. Caproni also fined Oren and Alon Alexander $300,000. She fined Tal Alexander $350,000.
It remains unclear whether the brothers will be housed together, as they requested. Caproni said she lacks the adequate expertise to make that call on her own, but said she will relay her concerns to the Bureau of Prisons that the men are “bad influences on one another.”
The trial sent shockwaves through the real estate industry, where Oren and Tal Alexander were luxury brokers to celebrity clients including Leon Black, Lindsay Lohan, Kim Kardashian and Kanye West. Alon Alexander was an executive at his family’s private security company.
Prosecutors sought life sentences for the brothers, citing the grisly nature of their crimes. In a sentencing submission, they noted that many assaults were filmed, including Oren Alexander’s rape of a “nearly comatose 17-year-old girl.”
One woman, testifying under the pseudonym Katie Moore, said she believes Alon Alexander drugged her after an NBA watch party hosted by actor Zac Efron. Despite drinking very little, she said she quickly lost control of her body and blacked out, later waking to a naked Alon Alexander standing over her.
“The first thing I said to him was, ‘I don’t want to have sex with you,’” Moore testified. “And his response was to laugh in my face and say, ‘You already did.’”
The government also noted that sexual assault accusations against the Alexanders date back to the early 2000s, when they were in high school.
“Tal, Alon, and Oren Alexander are finally being held accountable for their reprehensible actions against numerous women,” FBI Assistant Director in Charge James Barnacle said after Tuesday’s sentencing. “For years, they brazenly abused their power and resources to carry out predatory and deeply harmful sexual violence. Today marks the beginning of justice for the victims whose courage brought these crimes to light.”
The Alexanders’ lawyers sought 15-year sentences, portraying the brothers as family men and hardworking sons of immigrants. Each is a father, and Oren Alexander’s only child was born while he was in federal custody. The brothers have spent roughly two years at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn since their 2024 arrests.
Defense lawyers for the men said they expect to appeal the outcome of the case.

BREAKING NEWS | MUZIQUE MAGAZINE EXCLUSIVE
By Louisa Warwick | Reporting from inside Manhattan federal court | October 27, 2026
NEW YORK CITY — Tal, Oren and Alon Alexander were each sentenced to 30 years in federal prison on Tuesday, October 27, according to Muzique Magazine’s reporter inside the Manhattan courtroom. U.S. District Judge Valerie Caproni compared the three brothers to Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde as she addressed the evidence and imposed their sentences.
The announcement followed an emotional day of victim impact statements, including testimony that left some speakers in tears and drew applause from people in the courtroom.
Judge Valerie Caproni invokes Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
In remarks heard by Muzique Magazine’s courtroom reporter, Judge Caproni likened the brothers to Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, invoking a contrast between outward appearances and their conduct.
Discussing the women’s accounts, the judge said, according to the reporter’s contemporaneous notes: “Either all of those women are in the wrong line of work because they should all be actresses, or they were telling the truth and they were raped and drugged. And I credit latter.”
The quotation is attributed to firsthand courtroom reporting and has not yet been checked against an official transcript. Caproni’s remarks made clear that she credited the women’s testimony.
Tal, Oren and Alon Alexander each receive 30-year sentences
The three brothers received the same 30-year prison sentence, according to the sentences announced in court. The terms were below the life sentences sought by prosecutors and above the 15-year sentences requested by the defense.
Tal, Oren and Alon appeared in sand-colored prison uniforms during the proceedings. The brothers had been convicted in March 2026 in the federal sex-trafficking case.
Judge appears irritated during discussion of Tal Alexander’s DUI convictions
Earlier in the day, Tal Alexander’s attorney mentioned his two previous driving-under-the-influence convictions. Judge Caproni appeared annoyed during that exchange, according to Muzique Magazine’s reporter, who observed the discussion firsthand.
That description reflects the reporter’s impression of the judge’s demeanor, not a finding about her motives or the legal significance of the convictions.
Twelve victim impact statements and moments of applause
During the portion of the hearing observed by Muzique Magazine, 12 victim impact statements were delivered. Three speakers became visibly emotional and struggled to finish their remarks. Two statements prompted applause from people inside the courtroom.
The brothers remained largely hunched over as the women spoke and were not observed turning to look directly at the speakers during the statements witnessed by this reporter.
The proceedings brought the human impact of the case into focus before the judge announced the lengthy prison terms.
Victim describes eight-year-old daughter’s distress after discovering case online
In one of the victim impact statements, a woman described how her eight-year-old daughter searched for her mother on Google while attending a sleepover, according to Muzique Magazine’s firsthand courtroom reporting.
The mother told the court that her daughter did not understand what sex or sexual assault meant. As the child learned about the allegations involving her mother, she covered her ears with her hands and began crying, the woman said.
The victim told the court that the experience would affect both her and her daughter for the rest of their lives. Her account illustrated how the consequences described in the victim impact statements extended beyond the women themselves to their families and children.
Wives and parents not observed during portion of the hearing
Oren Alexander’s wife, Kamila Hansen Alexander, and Alon Alexander’s wife, Shani Zigron Alexander, were not identified by this reporter during the portion of the hearing attended. The brothers’ parents, Shlomy Alexander and Orly Alexander, were also not observed during that period.
This observation does not establish whether those family members attended another portion of the proceedings or were elsewhere in the courthouse.
From luxury real estate to decades in federal prison
Tal and Oren Alexander were prominent figures in luxury real estate, while Alon Alexander worked in the family’s private security business. Their convictions and sentencing have drawn extensive public attention.
Judge Caproni’s comparison to Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, her assessment of the women’s credibility and the equal 30-year prison sentences were among the defining developments of Tuesday’s hearing.
